leg.t: Utahns don’t want data centers, but they are coming. Here is how state lawmakers plan to get ‘only the best projects.’
leg.d: “Data centers will happen,” one lawmaker told reporters after the interim meeting. “But we can make sure that, in Utah, only the best projects that respect our natural resources, that benefit our local communities, happen.”

leg.t: Lawmakers’ plan would restrain Utah data center development — and MIDA
leg.d: Utah lawmakers facing intense outcry over data centers gave a first glimpse Wednesday of a wide-ranging plan to rein in development of the projects throughout the state.

leg.t: ‘Data centers will happen,’ so Utah lawmakers want to go big on new rules
leg.d: Utah lawmakers say a new proposal could address concerns over data center development, from water and energy use to local control and tax incentives, without imposing a statewide moratorium.

leg.t: New policies to regulate Utah data centers unveiled by lawmakers
leg.d: In response to significant public pushback, a draft policy has been unveiled on Utah's Capitol Hill seeking to regulate data centers.

leg.t: Bill proposes police training on investigating cases of missing, murdered Indigenous Utahns
leg.d: A bill will be introduced in the Utah State Legislature to offer training to police officers on better ways to investigate cases of missing and murdered Indigenous people.

leg.t: Utah legislator won’t get an intern or assigned staff after discrimination inquiry, records say
leg.d: Utah's Senate president said Sen. Kathleen Riebe, D-Cottonwood Heights, won’t get her own intern or staff based on findings of a discrimination inquiry, records show.

leg.t: Utah House Dems pick Jennifer Dailey-Provost as minority leader after midterm gains
leg.d: Dailey-Provost represents downtown Salt Lake City and says the election gives Democrats the opportunity to “show you can govern.”

leg.t: Fueled by Democratic gains, women will hold a record of state legislative seats

leg.t: With GOP supermajority gone, Utah Democrats have a bigger say in the Legislature
leg.d: With a larger caucus and new power to block constitutional amendments and veto overrides, Utah Democrats see an opportunity to change the tone of legislative debates.

leg.t: Data center regulation bills are coming, Utah's House Speaker says
leg.d: Bills regulating aspects of data centers are being drafted and will be introduced in the next legislative session, House Speaker Mike Schultz told FOX 13 News.
